question: In a melanoma study utilizing bulk rna seq, Prior to running DESeq2, an analyst filters out genes with fewer than 10 counts across at least 4 samples (the smallest group size), reducing the total tested genes from 35,000 to 18,000. How should this analysis be evaluated and executed?
proposed_analysis: Proposed analysis: Prior to running DESeq2, an analyst filters out genes with fewer than 10 counts across at least 4 samples (the smallest group size), reducing the total tested genes from 35,000 to 18,000.
preferred_analysis: Standard rigorous practice: Pre-filtering low-count genes reduces the multiple-testing penalty in Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and removes uninformative high-noise Poisson background.
reasoning_summary: Rigorous scientific assessment for melanoma: Standard rigorous practice: Pre-filtering low-count genes reduces the multiple-testing penalty in Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and removes uninformative high-noise Poisson background.

supported_claims.statement: Experimental data for melanoma was generated under specified assay parameters.
